objective: Every VPC-attached backend function's inline policy gains a Deny on the six ENI actions, conditioned on lambda:SourceFunctionArn, so the function's own code cannot call them while the Lambda service still can (AWS Lambda guide, "Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC" -> required IAM permissions, which recommends this deny).
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: this spec's Director PR has merged, and the branch is cut from a main that holds it.
Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation. They fail today because no Deny statement exists on any backend function policy.

backendFunction in infra/lib/app-stack.ts adds, only when the function is in the VPC, a statement with Sid DenyVpcNetworkInterfacesFromFunctionCode, Effect Deny, exactly the same six actions as the VpcNetworkInterfaces statement (ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces, ec2:DescribeSubnets, ec2:DeleteNetworkInterface, ec2:AssignPrivateIpAddresses, ec2:UnassignPrivateIpAddresses), Resource "*".

That Deny's Condition is ArnLike on lambda:SourceFunctionArn = arn:<partition>:lambda:<region>:<account>:function:<stackName>-*, built from the stack's own partition, region, account and stackName tokens (the stack is Fanwire-App), never a hard-coded account id or region. A test asserts the synthesized condition value.

The Api, Media, Notifications, AccountDeletion, Migration and SportsDataLoad policies each hold both the VpcNetworkInterfaces Allow and the new Deny. The SportsDataRefresh policy (outsideVpc) and the OriginVerifyAuthorizer policy hold neither.
The existing VpcNetworkInterfaces Allow statement is unchanged: same Sid, Effect, six actions and Resource "*".

A test asserts that no backend function in Fanwire-App sets an explicit FunctionName, so CloudFormation's generated names keep the Fanwire-App- prefix the condition relies on (live names verified 2026-11-24: Fanwire-App-ApiF70053CD-..., Fanwire-App-MediaA721A567-..., Fanwire-App-Notifications87298708-..., Fanwire-App-AccountDeletionAB9EBB6B-..., Fanwire-App-MigrationC13A4580-..., Fanwire-App-SportsDataLoad2ADE39DD-...).

infra/test/iam-policy.test.ts: the lambda-vpc-eni entry still matches the Allow, and matches a Deny with those actions only when the Deny carries the lambda:SourceFunctionArn condition (a hygiene test feeds a Deny without the condition and asserts no entry matches it). The entry's reason mentions the deny.
The IAM gate passes in every domain mode, and allow-list hygiene ('every allow-list entry is still needed', 'the walker flags a wildcard it has not been told about') still passes.
No other statement, environment variable, trigger or resource changes. infra/iam/** is unchanged: an inline policy document edit needs no new CloudFormation execution permission.

The PR body carries the expected cdk diff: Fanwire-App only, six AWS::IAM::Policy resources modified (the Api, Media, Notifications, AccountDeletion, Migration and SportsDataLoad policies; the implementer confirms the list from synth), each gaining exactly one Deny statement. No other stack changes; no resource added, removed or replaced.

The PR body's manual steps, after the deploy: a signed-in GET /api/users/me returns 200 (the Api function still gets its ENIs and egress), and no backend function's log group shows an AccessDenied on an ec2: action.
npm run build, npm run lint, npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 and npm run synth pass in infra/. Nobody runs cdk deploy.

wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x00b-architecture-iam-gaps.md's lambda-vpc-eni entry states the deny is implemented, removes 'Not implemented; it is in TODO/02-backlog.md', and counts six VPC-attached functions (Api, Media, Notifications, AccountDeletion, Migration, SportsDataLoad), naming SportsDataRefresh and the origin-verify authorizer as outside the VPC.
